chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, who said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The one to whom two days are equal, is defrauded. The one to whom the last of his two days was the better, is envied. The one to whom the last of his two days was the worst, is cursed. The one who does not look forward to increasement (of quality) in himself, is going towards decrement, and the one who goes towards decrement, death is better for him than life.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'defrauded' or 'envied' in terms of daily spiritual progress according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define the spiritual state of the 'defrauded' (maghbun) through the metric of daily self-improvement. The Imam contrasts the 'happy' (maghbub) who ends each day better than it began with the 'cursed' who declines, warning that perceived stagnation is actually a subtle slide into deficiency. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *muhasaba* (self-accountability) as a continuous process rather than a static state of being.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Khalid, from his father, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Hisham bin Salem, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

The one to whom two days are equal, is defrauded. The one to whom the last of his two days was the better, is envied. The one to whom the last of his two days was the worst, is cursed. The one who does not look forward to increasement (of quality) in himself, is going towards decrement, and the one who goes towards decrement, death is better for him than life.
